Dough Intent Coverage: Caught

Report: /tmp/dough-intent-coverage-SEED-374.IToxHi/report.md

Story and revision: SEED-374#see-stale-test-duration-estimates, from .planning/seeds/SEED-374-stale-test-duration-estimates.md#see-stale-test-duration-estimates and .planning/slice-plans/649-see-stale-test-duration-estimates/PLAN.md, at 3e5577a4bff8ee789ea41b502ebd907e9a1df670.

Selected promise: any single unrecorded job already on trunk makes the duration list stale; the preview opens with the stale diagnosis and a count of one. This check covers the supplied-trunk-labels CLI path. It does not assess the default origin/main runnable-job discovery rewrite.

Fault: scripts/share-preview.mjs:164, the first-line emission condition in formatPreview, changed from “if (staleCount > 0)” to “if (staleCount > 1)”. The actual source has a separate refresh-step condition, which remained intact. This one-line threshold fault suppresses the diagnosis only at the one-job boundary. Maintained fixtures and assertions were unchanged.

Maintained proof: Distribution/tests/support/share-preview-stale.test.mjs, test “a single missing trunk job marks only its own share's headroom” (starts at line 155). Its assert.match at line 162 requires:
  /^Stale duration list .*: 1 job already on trunk lacks recorded seconds\.\n/

The caller's suggested test path was corrected to its actual maintained location under Distribution/tests/support/. All three runs selected this same file through:
  PATH=/opt/homebrew/bin:$PATH bash scripts/test.sh Distribution/tests/support/share-preview-stale.test.mjs
OPEN_DOUGH_TEST_TIMES retained runner durations; fault/restored runs also retained job and case outcomes. No dependency installation was needed: the isolated revision's focused baseline executed and passed without node_modules.

Evidence:
- Baseline: exit 0; selected file passed, runner time 0.3 seconds.
- Fault: exit 1; four cases passed and the one-job case failed. The actual catching assertion was the first-line/count assert.match at line 162, rather than the later affected-share assertions.
- Reach and wrong behavior: the failing maintained case's captured CLI output contained three jobs, two recorded, one unrecorded at 5.0 seconds; missing.sh was explicitly marked “(stale; assumed 5.0 s)”, and its share's headroom rested on assumed seconds. Its first line nevertheless began “Predicted job-seconds per share”, omitting the required stale diagnosis.
- Independent observation: an external scratch CLI fixture contained long.sh=9 seconds, short.sh=1 second, and unrecorded missing.sh, with all three labels supplied as trunk members, two shares and ceiling 30. The real scripts/test-shares.mjs preview command exited 0 with empty stderr before, during and after the fault. Before/after output opened “Stale duration list …: 1 job already on trunk lacks recorded seconds.” During the fault, it opened “Predicted job-seconds per share …: 3 jobs, 2 recorded, 1 unrecorded at 5.0 s each”; missing.sh still had its stale annotation. This independently establishes wrong behavior on the intended one-job path, matching the maintained case.
- Restored: original module bytes were restored in a finally block with signal handling. Pre-probe and restored porcelain status and binary diff were all empty; a final git diff --exit-code confirmed the module, maintained test and retained fixture unchanged. The same focused command passed again, exit 0, all five cases passed, runner time 0.2 seconds. Restored independent CLI output matched clean output byte for byte.

Next proof action: retain the maintained first-line/count assertion as evidence for this one-job boundary. This probe requires no assertion repair; wider proof decisions remain with the caller.

Prior disposition: the caller's separately planned CI optimization and one-time budget-failure landing/wrap-up exception are unchanged. This probe made no production optimization or repair decision. The deliberately introduced assertion failure was removed and the restored focused proof passed. Failure-policy reference: Distribution/src/skills/dough-execute-plan/references/failure-policy.md.
